Blount County, TN Tax Sales: Your Complete Guide to Buying Properties at Auction

Looking to buy property in Tennessee at a discount? Blount County might be the place for you. The county holds annual tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes. If the property owner doesn’t pay, their property could end up at auction. That’s where you come in.

Whether you’re a local or out-of-state investor, this guide breaks down everything you need to know about buying tax sale properties in Blount County, Tennessee.

How the Tax Sale Works in Blount County

  1. Check Listings
    Properties are listed on the Clerk & Master’s site and in the Daily Times newspaper.
  2. Register to Bid
    Registration opens on GovEase.
  3. Auction Day
    The auction goes live on 9:00 AM CST.
  4. Pay if You Win
    Winning bidders must pay the full amount using approved payment types.
  5. Redemption Period
    Original owners have 1 year to reclaim the property.
  6. Get the Deed
    If not redeemed, you receive the tax deed and can pursue full ownership.

Important Tax Sale Info: Blount County, TN

What You Need to Know Before Bidding

  • Sales Are Final – No refunds or cancellations after bidding.
  • As-Is Properties – No guarantees on condition or title.
  • There May Be Liens – Other debts may still be attached.
  • Redemption Period Applies – Wait 1 year before you take full control.
  • Legal Work Might Be Needed – Quiet title actions and evictions can come up.
  • Do Your Homework – Always research properties thoroughly.

Real Estate Facts About Blount County

Great Smoky Mountains Access
Properties near Townsend and park entrances are popular for vacation rentals.

Growth in Maryville & Alcoa
These cities are growing quickly thanks to strong schools and local jobs.

High Demand for Rentals
Families, retirees, and professionals all create demand for long-term rentals.

Urban + Rural Choices
Choose from farmland, wooded lots, or developed subdivisions.

Outdoor Lifestyle Sells
Access to rivers, trails, and mountain views keeps demand strong.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Can I attend the auction in person?
No. The sale is being held online through GovEase.

Can out-of-state buyers participate?
Yes. Anyone registered with GovEase can bid, no matter where they live.

Do I get the property right after I win?
Not right away—there’s a 1-year redemption period.

What if the property is occupied?
You may need to follow legal eviction procedures after the redemption period ends.

Can I buy properties that don’t sell at auction?
Sometimes, yes. Contact the Clerk & Master’s Office for over-the-counter opportunities.

Pro Tips for First-Time Buyers

  • Inspect what you can – Parcel maps and satellite photos help if you can’t visit in person.
  • Use certified funds – Cashier’s checks or money orders are typically required.
  • Stick to your budget – Set a bid limit before auction day.
  • Expect legal fees – Title clearing and quiet title actions may be necessary.
  • Wait to improve – You can’t use or fix up the property during the redemption period.

Why Blount County Is Great for Tax Deed Investors

  • Auctions are now easy to access online through GovEase.
  • The local market stays strong, thanks to its location near Knoxville.
  • It’s popular with both tourists and long-term residents.
  • Entry prices are often lower than nearby counties.
  • The 1-year redemption window offers balance between investor security and owner rights.
